criteria.rationale: The substantive document provides the requested first-level executive and TechSol workflow: modular quotations covering all four requested cost-driver categories; supplier evaluation, RFQ, negotiation and nomination; owners and gates; tiered post-nomination changes; mandatory approval layers; and digital traceability, visibility and configuration requirements. Purchase retains ownership of the nomination file. Affected-module delta pricing, frozen unaffected modules, parallel reviews, versioning and advance option pricing provide concrete flexibility points. Thresholds, approval time limits, targets and onboarding choices are appropriately left open for a first-level draft rather than invented. No substantive correction or unnecessary process hold is established. This is a content assessment: the 2–3-page limit, rendering and visual usability remain separate, unverified engineering checks.

evidence.source_quote: Clearly define the process steps, decision gates, approval layers, and flexibility points to handle post-nomination design changes.
evidence.output_quote: The workflow has seven steps. A gate is a point where the process stops until the stated criteria are met and recorded. Within each step, the platform records the owner, time stamp, documents and comments.

evidence.source_quote: allowing the purchase process to adapt flexibly to late-stage design changes without compromising traceability, stakeholder visibility, or project governance.
evidence.output_quote: When ER or the Program Manager updates a TRSO, the platform creates a change request. The request is linked to the original nomination, and it identifies the affected modules. Only the affected modules are re-quoted and re-negotiated. Unaffected modules stay frozen, which avoids reopening the whole nomination.
